tonnage_mt.note: Petroleum fields are sized by volume (millions of barrels of oil or oil equivalent), not ore tonnage. See extra.field_size_mmboe.

deposits_per_1e5_km2.where: DDS-60 chapters AM, AR, MC, GL and AU 71920101 searched
deposits_per_1e5_km2.note: No USGS density of oil or gas fields per area was found. The World Petroleum Assessment estimates NUMBERS of undiscovered fields per assessment unit (for example 200 / 580 / 1000 oil fields, min / median / max, for AU 71920101, extra.niger_delta_undiscovered_oil_field_count). The AU data form gives the AU's areal split by country as percentages, not its area.

min_separation_m.note: No distance rule. A field is 'a production unit consisting of a collection of oil and gas pools that when projected to the surface form an approximately contiguous area that can be circumscribed'. An oil field has GOR < 20,000 cfg/bbl; a gas field has GOR >= 20,000.

field_size_mmboe.where: p50: data form 'Size of Undiscovered Fields', median size, PDF p. 4; p90 and p10: 'Agbada Reservoirs, AU 71920101, Undiscovered Field-Size Distribution' bar chart (oil fields), PDF p. 7
field_size_mmboe.note: EXAMPLE ONLY: Niger Delta Province (7192), Tertiary Niger Delta (Agbada/Akata) TPS, Agbada Reservoirs assessment unit 71920101, USGS World Petroleum Assessment 2000. These are the USGS-assessed sizes (grown) of UNDISCOVERED OIL fields, in MMBO of oil only (the minimum-size cutoff is 1 MMBOE). p50 = 12 MMBO is printed in the data form. p90 and p10 were derived by this compiler: the eleven log2 size-class bars were measured at 250 dpi (heights 38.9, 83.1, 106.6, 111.3, 97.2, 71.3, 43.8, 22.5, 9.7, 3.6, 0.9 fields for 1-<2 ... 1024-<2048 MMBO; sum 589 vs the printed mean of 586.3), and the cumulative 10% and 90% points were interpolated log-linearly within a class. The same procedure gives p50 = 12.0, matching the data form. p10 reads 88-90 depending on outline handling. The input distribution is a shifted truncated lognormal (DDS-60 chap. MC) with min 1, median 12 and max 1500 MMBO (extra.niger_delta_*). For a small-field province see extra.uinta_*.

field_size_distribution_type.note: The Emc2 program used for the World Petroleum Assessment 2000 uses 'shifted truncated lognormal distributions for the field-size and triangular distributions for numbers of undiscovered fields and for coproduct ratios'. Inputs are given as minimum (F100), median (F50) and maximum (F0) fractiles (chap. AM, p. AM-6).

niger_delta_discovered_fields.note: Plus 93 discovered gas fields. Established AU (> 13 fields).

niger_delta_discovered_oil_field_median_.note: By discovery thirds: 1st 60, 2nd 21.6, 3rd 22.6 MMBOE. Discovered gas fields: 116 / 58 / 199 BCFG.

uinta_min_field_size_mmboe.note: Second example, a small-field province: Uinta Green River Conventional Oil and Gas AU (50200501), USGS National Oil and Gas Assessment 2002. 15 discovered oil fields >= 0.5 MMBO.

uinta_undiscovered_oil_field_size_mmbo.note: Number of undiscovered oil fields 1 / 6 / 12. Median size of discovered oil fields by thirds 2.15 / 2.19 / 1.2 MMBOE (also stated in the text, p. 27, PDF p. 31).

world_min_field_size_mmboe.unit: MMBOE (largest minimum field size used by any AU)
world_min_field_size_mmboe.where: chap. AR, 'Minimum Field Size', p. AR-32 (PDF p. 49); fig. AR-98
world_min_field_size_mmboe.note: 'No minimum field size exceeded 20 MMBOE. Seventy percent of minimum field sizes were in the range of 1 through 5 MMBOE.'

world_median_undiscovered_oil_field_size.where: chap. AR, 'Size of Undiscovered Fields', p. AR-33 (PDF p. 50); fig. AR-100
world_median_undiscovered_oil_field_size.note: Across the AUs of the assessment (the chapter speaks of 270 defined assessment units): about 45 percent were judged to contain undiscovered oil fields with a median size of 1-10 MMBO, and just under 20 percent a median size exceeding 30 MMBO. Similar for gas. Roughly half the AUs were judged to hold 1-25 undiscovered oil fields and about a quarter more than 50 (p. AR-33).

tti_onset_oil_generation.where: abstract, AAPG Bull. 64(6) p. 916 (via OSTI record 6845191)
tti_onset_oil_generation.note: Waples (1980) thresholds: 15 onset of oil generation; 75 peak; 160 end of oil generation; ~500 40-degree (API) oil preservation deadline; ~1000 50-degree oil deadline; ~1500 wet-gas preservation deadline; > 65,000 dry-gas preservation deadline. NOT found restated as 15/75/160 in a USGS document. USGS reports that use the method pick their own thresholds: PP 1698 uses TTI 10 for the onset of oil and ~160 for thermogenic gas, and draws TTI = 15, 60 and 160 lines on its burial plot; OFR 88-450-G uses 10 and 180 (extra.tti_usgs_*).

tti_peak_oil_generation.where: abstract, AAPG Bull. 64(6) p. 916 (via OSTI record 6845191)

tti_end_oil_generation.where: abstract, AAPG Bull. 64(6) p. 916 (via OSTI record 6845191)

tti_oil_40api_preservation_deadline.note: Printed as 'approx. 500'. The OSTI rendering says '40 deg'; this is presumably API gravity.

tti_dry_gas_preservation_deadline.note: Dry gas survives up to at least TTI 65,000.

tti_rate_doubling_interval_c.unit: degC per doubling of maturation rate
tti_rate_doubling_interval_c.note: 'The rate of the chemical reactions involved in thermal maturation ... appears to double with every 10 degC (18 degF) rise in temperature' (the basis of Lopatin's TTI).

tti_ro_correspondence_waples1981.note: NOT USGS. Kansas Geological Survey table, credited to Waples (1981): TTI 15 -> Ro 0.6 (onset of oil); TTI 75 -> Ro 1.1 (peak oil); TTI 160 -> Ro 1.3 (end of oil); TTI 1,500 -> Ro ~3.8 (upper TTI limit for wet gas). Waples' 1980 TTI-Ro table itself was not opened.

tti_usgs_pp1698_onset_oil.where: chap. B, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 29); Figure 11, printed p. 26 (PDF p. 33)
tti_usgs_pp1698_onset_oil.note: Wattenberg field, Denver Basin: 'Estimated onset of oil generation is at a TTI of 10 (vitrinite reflectance Ro 0.6 percent); generation of thermogenic gas occurs at a TTI of about 160 (Ro 1.3 percent)'. A calculated maximum TTI of 350 corresponds to Ro 1.6%. Figure 11 draws TTI = 15, 60 and 160 lines. p. 26 cites Waples (1980) for 'Ro 1.35 percent' as the minimum for thermogenic gas from oil breakdown.

tti_usgs_ofr88450g_oil_window.unit: Lopatin TTI (top and base of the oil window)
tti_usgs_ofr88450g_oil_window.where: 'Thermal maturation and burial history', PDF p. 10 (printed page number not legible); Piceance example PDF p. 13 (printed p. 10)
tti_usgs_ofr88450g_oil_window.note: 'The assumed top of the oil window is at a TTI of 10, and the base was assumed to be TTI 180', with a geothermal gradient of 1.5 degF per 100 ft assumed (Uinta Basin). At the MWX site the base (TTI 180) matches Ro > 1.35%.

ro_onset_oil_type_ii_pct.note: Citing Waples (1985): onset of oil generation from about 0.45-0.50% Ro for high-sulfur kerogen, 0.60% for type II and 0.65% for type III. The end of oil generation is 'commonly accepted' at 1.35% Ro. Type I (Dow, 1977) generates oil between 0.50 and 1.35%. Wet gas forms between 0.80 and 2.0% Ro, dry (thermogenic) gas between about 1.0 and 3.0%, and biogenic gas as low as 0.20% (peat). Figure 2 (PDF p. 5) marks 0.60, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.35% Ro.

ro_type_iii_gas_thresholds_pct.unit: percent Ro (onset of significant gas, maximum gas generation)
ro_type_iii_gas_thresholds_pct.note: Type III kerogen: Ro ~0.75% is the onset of significant gas generation and 1.10% the level of maximum generation and expulsion (Meissner, 1984, as cited). The upper limit for gas preservation may be as high as 3.5% (Dow, 1977) or 4.0% Ro (Waples, 1980, as cited). Wet gas forms at 0.80-2.0% Ro and dry gas at ~1.0-3.0% Ro.

oil_window_temperature_c.note: 'Assuming a geothermal gradient typical for a long-standing passive margin (~30 degC/km), the depth to the oil window (80 degC to 120 degC) ...' The ~50-150 degC catagenesis window was NOT found stated in a USGS document opened.

geothermal_gradient_passive_margin_c_per.note: 'typical for a long-standing passive margin (~30 degC/km)'.

geothermal_gradient_sedimentary_basins_c.note: 'Temperature gradients of 20-25 degC/km are common in sedimentary basins, and 30 degC/km is commonly assumed as the upper limit in models.' The report also uses a mean annual surface temperature of 15 degC.

geothermal_gradient_examples_f_per_100ft.where: PP 1698 chap. B printed p. 22 (PDF p. 29); OFR 88-450-G PDF p. 10
geothermal_gradient_examples_f_per_100ft.note: Wattenberg field (Denver Basin) about 2.55 degF/100 ft, and about 2.0 degF/100 ft outside the field (PP 1698). Uinta Basin model assumption 1.5 degF/100 ft (OFR 88-450-G). Converted by this compiler: 1.5, 2.0 and 2.55 degF/100 ft = 27, 36 and 46 degC/km.
